thread:
Alex: FYI seeing apiserver leader lag and controller-manager leader-election churn in eu-west-1 starting ~22:34 UTC. GPU provisioning API calls are timing out and capacity backfills stalled.
Maria: saw the same, kube-controller-manager logs show leader election timeouts + requeues.
Jin: link to grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123 -- apiserver p95 latency spikes correlated with NAT gateway flap earlier.
SRE-Oncall: incident bot reported NAT route flaps in eu-west-1 at 22:33:07. NetOpsBot: detected BGP withdraw/reannounce on poor-peering-3 (AS64512) 22:32:50-22:33:50 :warning:.
Alex: logs (snippet):
```
I0331 22:34:10.123456 1 leaderelection.go:258] error retrieving resource lock kube-system/kcm: timed out waiting for the condition
E0331 22:34:12.654321 1 controllermanager.go:270] Failed to sync GPUProvisioner: Context deadline exceeded
```
Maria: controller-manager fallback path kept retrying, causing a reconciliation storm that hit apiserver file-descriptors.
Jin: current apiserver FD usage: 92% (3300/3600) on api-1/eu-west-1, proxy pools saturated.
SRE-Oncall: immediate mitigation ideas?
Alex: short term: increase leader-election leaseDuration to 15s for controller-manager to avoid thrash, and temporarily scale APIServer replicas from 3 -> 5 in eu-west to absorb FD pressure.
Maria: agree on scale. Also disabled autoscale for GPU-provisioner job to stop thundering creates.
Jin: netops rolling fix: blackholed the flapping peer for 10m and rerouted traffic. BGP flaps stopped at 22:41.
SRE-Oncall: applied scaling, leader-election TTL bump, and disabled aggressive backoff in provisioner. APIServer latency p95 back to normal 22:44.
Alex: follow-ups: 1) add NAT/GW peer healthcheck to provisioning pipeline to fail early, 2) add kcm leader-election instrumentation to dashboards, 3) run a DR test for controller-manager leader churn.
Maria: cost note: scaling apiserver from 3->5 and extra retry suppression will increase infra cost ~0.8% for eu-west for 24h, approving since it prevents GPU job failures.
Jin: I filed a post-incident ticket and tagged infra/billing and netops: INC-4891.
SRE-Oncall: will monitor for 6h, reopening if we see FD >85% or leader re-election >3/min. :thumbsup:
Alex: nice catch everyone, looks like network flap induced leader-election cascade + controller reconciliation storm which blocked GPU provisioning path and increased short-term cost (gpu debt).
Maria: adding a runbook step to throttle controller-manager reconciliation on provisioner error spike.
Jin: pushing a small PR to improve provisioner backoff: https://git.internal/r/PR-9223
SRE-Oncall: logging the actions in incident channel, closing thread unless something new pops.
